title: Augmented presheaf bar resolution and evaluation contraction
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a small category and $R$ a commutative ring. Write $\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{op},\operatorname{Mod}_R)$; it is the module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] for the constant ring on the topology generated by singleton identities [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Derived categories and cochain complexes mean [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $U\in\mathcal E$ and an $R$-module $M$, put $L_U(M)(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}M$, with restriction along $b:W\to V$ sending $(a,m)$ to $(ab,m)$. For $F\in\mathcal A_{\mathcal E,R}$, let $B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}L_{U_n}(F(U_0))$ for $n\ge0$, with zero positive terms. On evaluation at $V$ its generators are $(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. The face $d_j$ deletes $U_{n-j}$, composing adjacent arrows (including $a$ when $j=0$); the last face restricts $x$ along $U_1\to U_0$. Use differential $\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^jd_j$ for $n>0$, and augmentation $a_F(a:V\to U_0,x)=F(a)x$ in degree zero. These formulas define an additive functorial augmented complex $a_F:B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)\to F[0]$, with the face identities $d_id_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$. At each fixed $V$, the augmented complex has the contraction $s_n(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)=(V\xrightarrow1 V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ and $s_{-1}(x)=(1_V,x)$; it satisfies $ds_n+s_{n-1}d=1$, including $ds_0+s_{-1}a_F=1$ and $a_Fs_{-1}=1$. No naturality of $s_n$ in $V$ is asserted. Thus $a_F$ is a quasi-isomorphism of presheaf complexes. Both $F\mapsto B_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$ and the complex $F\mapsto K_{\mathcal E,R}(F)$ defined by $K^{-n}=\bigoplus_{U_n\to\cdots\to U_0}F(U_0)$ with the same vertex-deletion faces (only the last face restricts the coefficient) preserve objectwise short exact sequences. With $C=\operatorname{colim}_{\mathcal E^{op}}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the natural isomorphism $b_F:CB(F)\cong K(F)$ is identity on coefficients of generators; its degree-zero map identifies $C(a_F^0)$ with $(U,x)\mapsto\iota_Ux$ into $CF$.

proof.text: All sums are small by smallness of $\mathcal E$. A summand is a copy of $F(U_0)$, so each prescribed face extends uniquely $R$-linearly to the sum. Restriction along $b:W\to V$ replaces $a$ by $ab$; identities and compositions follow from $(ab)c=a(bc)$. Faces commute with restriction: for the first face this is the same associativity equation; other faces leave $a$ alone, except the last, whose coefficient restriction commutes with these reindexings. Thus these are presheaf maps. A natural map $t:F\to G$ acts by $x\mapsto t_{U_0}x$. Its naturality makes it commute with the last face and augmentation; all other faces retain $x$. This action preserves identities, composition, sums of maps and zero maps.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), explicit presheaf-resolution expansion of the category bar complex.

proof.text: For $i<j$, deleting the two specified vertices in either order gives $d_i d_j=d_{j-1}d_i$. Nonadjacent deletions act independently. Adjacent deletions at internal vertices, or at the initial vertex next to $a$, agree by associativity of arrow composition. Two deletions at the coefficient end agree because $F(fg)=F(g)F(f)$; a coefficient-end deletion and any nonadjacent deletion commute because the latter leaves the coefficient unchanged. These cover all pairs. In $d^2$ the term indexed by $(i,j)$ with $i<j$ has sign $(-1)^{i+j}$ and pairs with $(j-1,i)$ of sign $(-1)^{i+j-1}$, so the terms cancel. In degree $-1$, on $(V\xrightarrow a U_1\xrightarrow f U_0,x)$ the two augmentation values are $F(fa)x$ and $F(a)F(f)x$, equal by contravariance. Therefore $a_Fd=0$, and the formulas give an augmented cochain complex with the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The identical deletion argument with the incoming arrow omitted proves $d^2=0$ for $K(F)$ as well.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), explicit presheaf-resolution expansion of the category bar complex.

proof.text: Fix $V$. Inserting $1_V$ defines $R$-linear maps $s_n$ on each summand. For $n\ge1$ one has $d_0s_n=1$ and $d_js_n=s_{n-1}d_{j-1}$ for $1\le j\le n+1$: deleting the inserted vertex recovers the generator, and deleting any other vertex performs the old deletion with its index increased by one, including the coefficient restriction at the last vertex. Hence $ds_n=1-s_{n-1}d$. For $n=0$, the two faces of $(V\xrightarrow1 V\xrightarrow a U_0,x)$ are $(a,x)$ and $(1_V,F(a)x)$, giving $ds_0=1-s_{-1}a_F$. Finally $a_Fs_{-1}(x)=F(1_V)x=x$. This proves every stated contraction identity, solely at the fixed evaluation object.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), explicit presheaf-resolution expansion of the category bar complex.

proof.text: For a cycle $z$ in negative degree of $B(F)(V)$, the contraction gives $z=d(sz)$, so its cohomology vanishes. In degree zero, the augmentation is surjective with section $s_{-1}$, and $z\in\ker a_F$ satisfies $z=ds_0z$; conversely $a_Fd=0$. Thus $H^0(a_F(V))$ is bijective. Positive degrees are zero. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact], which computes presheaf homology objectwise and detects its isomorphisms by evaluations. The augmentation therefore induces isomorphisms of all cohomology presheaves, and is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), explicit presheaf-resolution expansion of the category bar complex.

proof.text: For an objectwise short exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$, each term of $K$ is a direct sum of the corresponding module sequences at $U_0$; each evaluation of a term of $B$ is another such sum, also indexed by $a:V\to U_n$. A sum of injections is injective by coordinates. An element in the middle kernel has finitely many nonzero coordinates; lift each of those coordinates to $F'(U_0)$ to obtain a preimage of finite support. Similarly lift the finitely many coordinates of any element of the last sum to $F(U_0)$, proving surjectivity. Thus both constructions give degreewise short exact sequences (also in the zero positive degrees), and their maps commute with differentials by step 1.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), explicit presheaf-resolution expansion of the category bar complex.

proof.text: For each $n$, send $(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ to $(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)\in K^{-n}(F)$. These maps form a cocone, since restriction only changes $a$. Given any cocone $\mu_V:B(F)^{-n}(V)\to M$, its unique factorization sends $(U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$ to $\mu_{U_n}(U_n\xrightarrow1 U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. Indeed the cocone relation along $a:V\to U_n$ identifies this with $\mu_V(V\xrightarrow a U_n\to\cdots\to U_0,x)$. The identity summands also force uniqueness. Thus $K^{-n}(F)$ satisfies the colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], giving $b_F^{-n}:CB(F)^{-n}\cong K^{-n}(F)$. Its inverse sends each generator to the colimit class of its identity-summand representative.

source.place: Tag 08PG (example-left-derived-colimits), explicit presheaf-resolution expansion of the category bar complex.

proof.text: The maps $b_F^{-n}$ commute with each face: deleting the first vertex forgets $a$ and the first arrow on either side, an internal deletion composes the same arrows, and the last deletion restricts $x$ along the same arrow. Thus they give the complex isomorphism $b_F:CB(F)\cong K(F)$. Both $b_F$ and its inverse commute with $t:F\to G$ since they retain the coefficient. Finally, in degree zero $C(a_F^0)$ sends the class of $(V\xrightarrow a U,x)$ to $\iota_VF(a)x=\iota_Ux$ by the colimit cocone relation for $F$. This is exactly the asserted normalized augmentation into $CF$.
